A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same paper. Their main sections, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results and Expedia hotel-search analyses, including estimation errors, confidence-interval coverage, runtime comparisons, and ranking-position effects.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and hotel-search results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The causal-parametrisation maximum-likelihood estimator and reduced-parametrisation estimator are unchanged, including their inputs, computation, and clipping procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic causal models and Expedia hotel-ranking tasks, including the fixed-hotel analysis across positions 1–20. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same Oracle, NoAdj, NoAdj*, WAdj, and WAdj* comparators appear in the corresponding simulation and hotel comparisons; the fixed-hotel analysis retains Oracle and NoAdj*. The newly cited Prashant et al. method is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Simulation sample sizes, domain configurations, evaluation metrics, hotel-selection rules, price discretisation, and the 25-source/18-target hotel experiment remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Condition-number sensitivity, sample-size and source-domain analyses, interval-coverage comparisons, runtime analysis, and the ranking-position case study are retained unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: Simulation repetition counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including asymptotic and bootstrap intervals, coverage levels, and the Wald and exact-binomial intervals used in the hotel analyses.

E6.justification: The result plots and numerical findings are unchanged. Examples include simulation mean absolute errors of 0.040 and 0.058 for the causal and reduced estimators in Section 5.2, and the reduced estimator's hotel-data error of 0.044 in Section 6.

T1.justification: The assumptions, identifiability results, consistency and asymptotic-normality propositions, proofs, counterexample, and extensions in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Citation renumbering and equation spacing do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about identifying target-domain causal effects from proxies, constructing two consistent estimators, and supporting them empirically.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain unchanged, including sensitivity to ill-conditioned probability matrices, bootstrap coverage-versus-length tradeoffs, hotel-data dependencies, and continuous latent confounders as future work.

D1.justification: The code and dataset access information and implementation details are unchanged, including R's L-BFGS-B optimisation and the 50,000-iteration limit in Appendix C.2. The added correspondence line supplies author contact information.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Prashant et al. (2025), Scalable out-of-distribution robustness in the presence of unobserved confounders, and describes its latent-shift approach using approximate confounder identification. Existing cited works are retained; subsequent reference numbers shift.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short related-work discussion and a correspondence address, with citation-number and bibliography-formatting updates. The remaining prose and section/appendix organisation are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions produce small spacing adjustments on the opening pages and reference-list reflow. All twelve figures and Table 1 retain their content and structure; the empirical plots and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added discussion of Prashant et al. in Section 1.1 modestly improves coverage of closely related latent-shift approaches and clarifies their use of approximate confounder identification. The methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and reproducibility material remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
